title: Hype, FOMO and rug pulls
hook: Everyone at school is talking about a new coin. A video says it went up 500% this week and "it's not too late". You feel like you're missing out.
card1: That feeling has a name: FOMO, the fear of missing out. Hype is built to make you feel it, because people who feel rushed don't stop to check.
analogy1: Hype is like a crowd running towards a shop. You start running too without knowing why. Sometimes there's a sale. Sometimes the people at the front are the ones selling.
card2: Crypto prices have high [[volatility]]. A coin can double in a week and lose 90% the next. Often the people who promoted it sell first.
card3: In a [[rug-pull]], the creators of a coin hype it up, collect buyers' money and then disappear with it. The price falls to almost zero, often within minutes.

story.title: The coin named after a TV show
story.body: In late October 2021, a new coin called SQUID was launched, named after the hit series Squid Game, although the show's makers had nothing to do with it. Its price shot up from about a cent to around 2,800 US dollars by 1 November. But buyers found they could not sell. Then the anonymous creators vanished with about 3.38 million dollars, and the price crashed to almost zero within minutes.
story.question: Which warning signs could buyers have spotted?
story.answer: The creators were anonymous, the coin used a famous name it had no right to, the price rose impossibly fast, and buyers reported that they couldn't sell. If you can't get out, it isn't an investment. It's a trap.

adviceIntro: A video about a new coin gets millions of views. Which lines would you not follow?

l1.text: Put in all your savings. You only live once!
l1.why: Never put in more than you can afford to lose completely. Prices can fall to zero.

l2.text: Borrow money from friends to buy more now.
l2.why: If the price falls, you lose the coins and still owe the money.

l3.text: Only use money you could lose without it hurting.
l3.why: Crypto prices can crash. Using only what you can afford to lose keeps you safe.

l4.text: Never sell, even if it crashes. Diamond hands!
l4.why: Slogans like this keep buyers in while the promoters sell. Make your own plan.

l5.text: Check who made the coin and whether you can actually sell it.
l5.why: Anonymous creators and coins you can't sell are classic signs of a rug pull.

hype.prompt: A friend says: "This coin is going up 50% a day! Put your birthday money in now, before it's too late!"

all.label: Put all your birthday money in
all.before: You will spend all your birthday money on the coin.
all.what: Two days later the creators sold their coins and the price dropped 95%. Your birthday money is almost all gone.
all.why: When a price rises that fast, it's often hype, and the people who started it sell to latecomers.
all.how: The price only goes up while new buyers keep coming. When they stop, it can collapse.
all.realLife: Never put in money you can't afford to lose, and never because someone says "now or never".

little.label: Put in a little, just to try
little.before: You will put a small part of your money in.
little.what: The price crashed and your small amount is almost gone. It hurt less, but it's still lost.
little.why: Spending less limits the damage, but it doesn't make a bad coin good.
little.how: Even small buys add to the money that early sellers take out.
little.realLife: Keeping amounts small is wise. Checking the coin first is wiser.

research.label: Wait and check the coin first
research.before: You will look up who made the coin and whether people can sell it.
research.what: You found anonymous creators and reports that people can't sell. You kept your money.
research.why: Real chances don't disappear in a day. Taking time to check protects you from hype.
research.how: Hype works by rushing people. Slowing down breaks the trick.
research.realLife: Ask: who made it, can I sell it, and what happens if it goes to zero?

q1.prompt: A coin is up 500% this week and everyone is talking about it. What is the smart move?
q1.a: Buy now before you miss out
q1.b: Slow down and check who made it and whether you could sell it
q1.c: Buy, because if everyone talks about it, it must be safe
q1.explanation: FOMO and hype push you to act fast. Slowing down to check is what protects you.

q2.a: Creators hype a coin, take buyers' money and disappear
q2.b: A normal small dip in price
q2.c: Something that only happens to tiny coins nobody has heard of
q2.explanation: In a rug pull, the people behind a coin cash out and vanish, leaving buyers with coins that are worth almost nothing.

q3.prompt: How much should you put into a risky coin?
q3.b: Borrow some extra, since the price will go up
q3.c: Only what you could lose completely without it hurting
q3.explanation: Crypto prices can fall to zero. Only use money you can afford to lose, and never borrow to buy.

misc.fomoBuy: "If I don't buy now, I'll miss out forever." Hype is built to make you feel that. Real chances give you time to check.
misc.popularSafe: "If everyone talks about it, it must be safe." Popular isn't the same as safe. Rug pulls depend on crowds.
misc.normalDip: "A rug pull is just a normal dip." It's a scam: the creators take the money and vanish.
misc.onlyBigCoins: "Only tiny coins nobody knows get rug-pulled." SQUID was all over the news before it collapsed.
misc.allIn: "Go all in for the biggest win." The bigger the bet, the more you can lose.
misc.borrow: "Borrowing is fine if the price will go up." No one knows that. If it falls, you still owe the money.

t1: Hype and FOMO are built to rush you. Slow down and check.
t2: Only use money you could lose completely. Never borrow to buy.
t3: Anonymous creators and coins you can't sell are signs of a [[rug-pull]].
talk1: Have you ever bought something because everyone else had it? How did it turn out?
talk2: If you had 50 euros, how much would you feel OK losing completely?
